get.summary: List the open updates of this WordPress installation
get.description: Live read on every call (no cache): wp-cli on the installation reports plugin and theme updates and the offered WordPress core version. plugins and themes list only updates that are open right now, sorted by slug, at most 200 entries each; entries whose slug the update endpoint could not address are left out. core.current is the installed version known from the hosting inventory (null if unknown); core.available is null if no core update is offered. If the state cannot be read the answer is 502 updates_unavailable, never an empty list. Only for WordPress sites (422 capability_unavailable otherwise).

post.description: Queues one job (202 + Operation kind updates:run). Body: 1 to 5 items {type: plugin|theme, slug}, no duplicates; WordPress core is not supported (a request with a core key or an item of type core is rejected with 422 core_update_not_supported, more than 5 items with 422 too_many_items). Rejected up front without a job: 422 item_not_installed (an item is not installed), 422 backup_limit_reached (the installation has reached its backup limit; delete a backup first), 502 updates_unavailable. The job takes exactly one safety backup, then updates the items one by one and reads each version back. The operation result is {safety_backup: file name or null, items: [{type, slug, from, to, status}]} with status updated, unchanged, failed, skipped or unconfirmed; it is also present on failed and unknown operations. Job budget 360 s from the start of the handler (the safety-backup wait is part of it); an item is only started with at least 180 s left (120 s update call + 60 s read-back), otherwise it is skipped and the operation ends failed with time_budget_exhausted. Failed codes: safety_backup_pending / safety_backup_failed (no update was started), backup_limit_reached, daily_limit, item_not_installed, update_failed, time_budget_exhausted. An unconfirmed result ends unknown. Daily limit 30 runs per account, shared with the AI access.

delete.description: Irreversible. The backup is removed from the WordPress installation as an asynchronous operation (kind backups:delete). backup_id is the id returned by GET /sites/{site_id}/backups (path-encoding of + and : is optional). Two rules protect the site: the newest backup is never deleted (422 backup_protected), and no backup is deleted while a backup is being created or its outcome is unclear (422 backup_in_use). Both rules are checked when the request arrives and again when the operation runs; in the second case the operation ends as failed with the same error_code. An unknown id is 404 backup_not_found. A repeated request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same operation and never deletes twice. The result of a succeeded operation is {filename, remaining_backups, deletion_verified: true}; if the deletion could not be confirmed, the operation ends as unknown.

delete.description: Addressed through the LIVE site, which must be a target of the token (the staging site need not be). confirm must equal the host of the staging site exactly (ASCII; IDN hosts in punycode). The staging copy is found only by the staging rule (host staging.<main domain>, same package); the live site can never be deleted. Rejected up front: 404 staging_not_found, 422 confirmation_mismatch, 422 staging_in_use (a backup or update is open). Result of a succeeded operation: {staging_host, deleted: true, subdomain_removed}. An unconfirmed result ends unknown. Daily limit 5 per account, shared with the AI access.

post.description: Queues one job (202 + Operation kind staging:create) that creates the one staging copy `staging.<main domain>` of the LIVE site (a staging site cannot be the source; the site must be a target of the token). Body: {} only; the name is fixed and cannot be chosen. Runs in the WP-Cockpit worker (see the delegation notes) under the shared site lock with a reservation: subdomain, clone (WP Toolkit), read-back of the new installation, best-effort SSL. Rejected up front without a job: 422 capability_unavailable (a staging site), 422 no_live_instance, 409 staging_exists (a copy exists, or the subdomain staging.<main domain> already exists without a copy, for example left by a refused clone: remove it in the panel or ask Support, DELETE /sites/{site_id}/staging cannot because there is no installation; this check costs no daily limit), 422 storage_insufficient (the webspace measurably has too little room; an unmeasurable quota is not a refusal), 502 preparation_failed (the subdomain could not be checked; nothing was changed), 409 site_busy, 429 daily_limit (the API enforces 3 a day and account; creations through chat, MCP and Cockpit count on the same counter, and API creations count against their limit of 5), 503 delegation_unavailable. Result on success {staging_host, ssl: issued|failed|unconfirmed, staging_site_id: site id or null}. staging_site_id is the id to select when you issue a token for the new site (null when it could not be determined; it then appears in the token form after the sites are refreshed). The new site is not a target of existing tokens. failed clone_failed: WP Toolkit refused the clone, the empty subdomain stays (result {staging_host, subdomain_left: true}) and has to be removed in the panel or by Support; until then every new request is refused up front as staging_exists without using the daily limit. unknown clone_unconfirmed: the clone was started but the new installation was not seen; the site stays locked until Support settles it. Other unknown codes: staging_outcome_unknown (the answer of Plesk to the subdomain creation was a connection error or not clearly readable; the subdomain may exist and the site stays locked until Support has settled it), effect_uncertain, worker_lost, backend_timeout, unconfirmed_result. Failed before any change (the site is not locked afterwards): staging_exists, storage_insufficient, preparation_failed (an error before the first step), subdomain_creation_failed (only for a clear error message of Plesk), daily_limit, site_busy, service_unavailable, access_removed, token_inactive, api_unavailable, delegation_not_started, job_expired. There is no safety backup (nothing of the live site is changed).

post.description: Queues one job (202 + Operation kind backups:restore) that overwrites the site with a backup. OVERWRITES the website: everything written after the backup is lost (for scope full or database that includes WooCommerce orders and customers). The job runs in the WP-Cockpit worker, takes exactly one safety backup first and restores only when that backup is confirmed. Body: scope (required): full = the whole backup as a WP Toolkit restore task, database = only the database, files = only the files (newer files stay, wp-config.php is never replaced), folder = one wp-content folder, mirrored to the state of the backup (files not in the backup are deleted from that folder); folder (required with scope folder only): wp-content/uploads, wp-content/plugins/<slug> or wp-content/themes/<slug>; confirm_host (required): the exact host of this site (restores overwrite); confirm_data_loss (boolean, default false): must be true for scope full or database when WooCommerce is active on the site (an unreadable plugin list counts as active). backup_id must be a backup of this very installation (a staging copy's backups are only restorable through the staging site). Rejected up front without a job: 400 invalid_scope / invalid_folder / invalid_arguments, 403 permission_denied, 404 backup_not_found, 422 confirmation_mismatch, woo_confirmation_missing, backup_limit_reached (delete a backup first), backup_in_use, service_unavailable, 409 site_busy (another operation, automatic update, support lock or reservation on the subscription), 429 daily_limit (3 full and 3 partial restores per day and account, shared with the AI access), 503 delegation_unavailable. Result {safety_backup: file name or null, scope, restore_task: succeeded|pending|unknown|failed (full only), health_check: ok|issue_found|not_run (partial only)}; present on succeeded and, where it applies, on failed and unknown operations. succeeded: full needs the restore task seen succeeded; partial needs the finished import and a health check answer (issue_found is still succeeded: the site was restored, a check found a problem; the safety backup is the way back). A full restore whose WP Toolkit task is still running when the job ends stays running while the API polls the task (at most 30 minutes), then ends succeeded, failed restore_failed or unknown restore_pending (the site unlocks itself when the task ends). failed restore_failed: the import tool reported errors, the site may be partly restored (restore the safety backup). unknown (restore_outcome_unknown, restore_pending, effect_uncertain, worker_lost, backend_timeout, unconfirmed_result): the outcome is unclear, check the site; the site stays locked until the outcome is settled (partial restores: until Support releases it). Failed before any change: backup_not_found, confirmation_mismatch, woo_confirmation_missing, backup_limit_reached, safety_backup_pending, safety_backup_failed, daily_limit, site_busy, service_unavailable, backup_unsafe, backup_unreadable, no_database_in_backup, no_files_in_backup, folder_not_in_backup, siteurl_mismatch, siteurl_unreadable, time_budget_exhausted, delegation_not_started, job_expired. There is no automatic rollback.

post.description: OVERWRITES THE LIVE SITE with its staging copy (files, database, or selected tables), irreversibly except by restoring the safety backup. The site must be the LIVE site of the pair and must be a target of the token; the staging copy is found by the server (host staging.<main domain>), never named in the request. Body: scope (required) all|files|db|selected; tables (required with selected only, 1 to 1000 distinct names [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64} that exist in the staging database); delete_missing_files (required, boolean; true only with scope all or files: files on live without a counterpart in staging are deleted); confirm_host (required): the exact host of the live site; confirm_data_loss (boolean, default false): must be true for scope all or db when WooCommerce is active on live (an unreadable plugin list counts as active); dry_run (boolean, default false). Nothing else is accepted. dry_run=true answers 200 and does nothing to the site: no job, no Idempotency-Key needed, no idempotency entry, no daily counter, no backup, no lock. Data: {dry_run, scope, delete_missing_files, pair:{staging_host, live_host}, woocommerce_active: true|false|null, tables: staging tables (at most 1000) or null, missing_tables (selected tables not in staging), backup_quota:{used, limit}|null, storage_ok: true|false|null, busy: null|operation_running|cockpit_busy, daily_limit_reached, staging_newer_than_live: null (not determined)}. A dry run reads synchronously on the server (instance list, table list, plugin list for WooCommerce, storage check), is limited only by the general request limit, and like every POST answers 503 api_draining while the API is drained for maintenance. In a dry run confirm_host, delete_missing_files and confirm_data_loss are optional and only informative. Otherwise queues one job (202 + Operation kind staging:push). It runs in the WP-Cockpit worker (see the delegation notes) under the shared site lock with a reservation, takes exactly one safety backup of the LIVE site first and copies only when that backup is confirmed with its exact file name, then clears the cache and runs a health check of the live site. Rejected up front without a job: 400 invalid_scope / invalid_arguments, 403 permission_denied, 404 staging_not_found, 409 staging_ambiguous, 422 no_live_instance (also: a staging site), confirmation_mismatch, woo_confirmation_missing, unknown_table, backup_limit_reached, backup_in_use, service_unavailable, 409 site_busy, 429 daily_limit (5 a day and account, shared with the panel), 502 tables_unreadable, 503 delegation_unavailable. Result {safety_backup:{filename, created_at}, health_check: ok|issue_found|not_run, scope, delete_missing_files}; present on failed and unknown operations where it applies (health_check only on success). succeeded needs the named safety backup and a health check answer; issue_found is still succeeded (the copy happened, the check found a problem; the safety backup is the way back). failed copy_failed: WP Toolkit reported the copy failed after the live site may have been partly changed; restore the safety backup. unknown (copy_outcome_unknown, effect_uncertain, backup_outcome_unknown, worker_lost, backend_timeout, backend_job_missing, unconfirmed_result): the outcome is unclear, check the live site; the site stays locked until Support settles it. unknown site_binding_changed: the copy was proven and a fresh read shows that the live installation identity changed, so the public site_id no longer matches it (only then); the site is NOT locked; check the site and request a new token if needed. unknown binding_unconfirmed: the copy was proven but the binding could not be read right afterwards; the site is NOT locked; check the site. A token revoked, rights changed or the API switched off while the copy ran leave the proven result succeeded. The staging copy is not bound to an instance when the request is accepted: if it is deleted and recreated before the job runs, the new copy is pushed (own package only; use dry_run right before). Failed before any change to live: confirmation_mismatch, woo_confirmation_missing, pair_changed, unknown_table, tables_unreadable, backup_limit_reached, safety_backup_failed, time_budget_exhausted, daily_limit, site_busy, service_unavailable, access_removed, token_inactive, api_unavailable, delegation_not_started, job_expired. Two codes report failed but leave the site LOCKED (nothing was copied to live): safety_backup_pending (the safety backup still runs; the site stays reserved until that task is settled) and backup_filename_unavailable (the backup was made but its exact file name could not be determined; the reservation stays unknown until Support releases it). There is no automatic rollback.
